steps.note: `npx -y @hawkeyexl/manni meta validate "docs/**/*.md" --format json`: one object with `summary` and `results`.
`manni meta get title,tags docs/intro.md` reads the named fields.
For scripting, `get title,tags "docs/**/*.md" --format json`: one object per file with `file`, `present`, `values`.
Reach into nested metadata with dot-notation: `get author.name,tags.0 docs/intro.md`.
Extract one field across a tree: `get type "docs/**/*.md" --format json` (the page pipes it into jq).

must_not: Treat the TypeScript `runValidate` sample as a command to run. It is library code, and `@hawkeyexl/manni` is not installed as a dependency in the workspace.
Depend on `jq`. It is not installed here, so a step that pipes into it fails; check the JSON manni prints instead.
scaffolding: docs/intro.md carries `title: Introduction`, `tags: [onboarding, guide]` and a nested `author` (`name: Jane`), so the page's get commands print values. docs/bad-timestamp.md fails on `timestamp`, so the json report has a failing result, and docs/no-frontmatter.md has no metadata block (`present: false`). No config. jq is not on PATH, so the jq pipelines are scored by their manni half only. Doc Detective runs runShell through Git Bash here, which rewrites a leading-slash argument to a Windows path even when quoted, so the page's `get '/author/name' docs/intro.md` exits 2; the reference puts the pointer after another field (`author.name,/author/name`).
